sentences.text: Teams adopting Agile face an immediate choice: Scrum or Kanban?

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: The question appears simple, but the answer shapes how teams work, plan, and deliver software.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Choose wrong, and you'll fight the framework instead of benefiting from it.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Choose right, and the framework amplifies your team's effectiveness.↵The debate between Scrum and Kanban generates strong opinions.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Scrum advocates praise its structure and predictability.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Kanban proponents value its flexibility and flow.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Both camps claim their approach is "more Agile." The truth is more nuanced: neither framework is universally superior.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Each excels in different contexts, and many successful teams blend elements from both.↵This exploration cuts through the dogma to examine what Scrum and Kanban actually do, when each works best, and how to choose—or combine—frameworks for your specific situation.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Drawing from teams that succeeded and failed with both approaches, we'll uncover the real differences that matter.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Before comparing frameworks, understanding what each actually provides is essential.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Scrum and Kanban aren't just different flavors of the same thing—they represent fundamentally different approaches to managing work.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Scrum organizes work into fixed-length iterations called sprints:↵Scrum creates predictability through its rhythmic structure of fixed-length sprints, typically two weeks, where teams commit to delivering specific work.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: This time-boxed approach forces regular decision points—what to build, how to build it, and whether it's working.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: The commitment isn't just to complete tasks; it's a promise to deliver working software that stakeholders can see, touch, and provide feedback on.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Sprint boundaries create natural synchronization points for the entire organization: developers know when to integrate their work, product owners know when to expect demos, and stakeholders know when they'll see progress.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: This rhythm transforms chaotic development into a predictable cadence where everyone understands the tempo.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: The commitment aspect matters because it drives focus—once a sprint starts, the team protects that commitment by saying no to new requests and yes to finishing what they started.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: This combination of rhythm and commitment is what makes Scrum feel structured compared to more fluid approaches, providing guardrails that help teams new to Agile or those needing coordination across multiple groups.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Scrum's iterative nature aligns perfectly with MVP development—each sprint delivers a potentially shippable increment, allowing teams to build, measure, and learn in short cycles, validating assumptions before investing heavily in the *wrong direction*.↵:::anote{title="MVP in Scrum Context"}↵**Minimum Viable Product (MVP)** is the smallest version of a product that delivers value and enables learning.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: In Scrum, each sprint can deliver a mini-MVP—a working increment that tests assumptions and gathers feedback.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Rather than building everything upfront, teams use sprints to validate ideas incrementally, pivoting or persevering based on what they learn.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: This approach minimizes waste by ensuring you're building the right thing before committing to full development.↵**Scrum Core Elements**↵:::↵:::anote{title="⏱️ Time-Boxing"}↵Fixed sprint length (typically 2 weeks)↵Sprint starts with planning↵Sprint ends with review and retrospective↵Rhythm creates predictability↵Time-boxing forces decisions and prevents endless deliberation.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Without a deadline, teams can spend weeks perfecting features that users don't need.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: The fixed sprint length creates urgency—you have two weeks to deliver something valuable, so you focus on what matters most.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: This constraint breeds creativity and prioritization.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Teams learn to break work into sprint-sized chunks, which naturally leads to incremental delivery.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: The predictable rhythm also helps stakeholders plan around your releases, building trust through consistency.↵Scrum's time-boxes enable powerful predictability tools like burndown charts, which show remaining work versus time, making it obvious whether the team will finish on schedule.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: When a burndown chart trends upward instead of down, the team knows immediately they're in trouble and can adjust.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Velocity—the average story points completed per sprint—emerges from this rhythm, allowing teams to forecast how many sprints a feature will take.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: This predictability transforms vague promises into concrete commitments stakeholders can rely on.↵ ↵This burndown chart shows a healthy sprint where actual progress (solid blue line) tracks close to the ideal burndown (dashed green line).

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: The team started with 50 story points and steadily completed work each day.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: If the actual line had trended upward or flatlined, it would signal problems—scope creep, blocked work, or underestimated complexity.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: The visual makes sprint health obvious at a glance, enabling early intervention when things go off track.↵:::↵:::anote{title="🤝 Commitment"}↵Team commits to sprint scope↵Scope frozen during sprint↵Focus on completing committed work↵Velocity emerges from completed work↵Commitment creates focus by protecting the team from constant interruptions.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: When the team commits to a sprint scope, they're saying "we'll finish this, and we need you to let us focus." This social contract prevents the chaos of constantly shifting priorities mid-sprint.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: The frozen scope isn't about rigidity—it's about giving the team space to do deep work without context switching.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Over time, completed commitments build velocity data, which enables realistic planning.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Teams that honor their commitments build credibility with stakeholders, earning the autonomy to work effectively.↵:::↵:::anote{title="👥 Roles"}↵Product Owner: Prioritizes backlog↵Scrum Master: Facilitates process↵Development Team: Delivers work↵Clear roles prevent confusion about who decides what.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: The Product Owner owns the "what"—which features matter most and why.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: The Development Team owns the "how"—technical decisions and implementation.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: The Scrum Master owns the "how we work"—facilitating ceremonies and removing obstacles.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: This separation prevents the common dysfunction where everyone has opinions about everything but no one has clear authority.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: When roles blur, teams waste time in endless debates.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: When roles are clear, decisions happen quickly and work flows smoothly.↵:::↵:::anote{title="🎭 Ceremonies"}↵Sprint Planning: Select work for sprint↵Daily Standup: Synchronize team↵Sprint Review: Demo completed work↵Sprint Retrospective: Improve process↵Ceremonies provide structure for communication without requiring constant meetings.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Sprint Planning aligns the team on goals before work begins, preventing wasted effort.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Daily Standups catch problems early when they're still small—a 15-minute sync can prevent days of rework.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Sprint Reviews create feedback loops with stakeholders, ensuring you're building the right thing.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Retrospectives turn experience into improvement, making each sprint better than the last.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: These ceremonies aren't bureaucracy—they're investments that save far more time than they cost by preventing miscommunication and misalignment.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Kanban focuses on visualizing work and optimizing flow:↵:::anote{title="Visualization"}↵Board shows all work↵Columns represent workflow stages↵Cards move through stages↵Bottlenecks become visible↵Visualization makes invisible work visible, transforming abstract tasks into tangible cards everyone can see.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: When all work appears on a shared board, hidden bottlenecks become obvious—you can literally see where cards pile up.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: This transparency prevents the common problem where everyone is busy but nothing gets finished.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Team members can glance at the board and understand the current state without status meetings.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Visualization also creates shared ownership—the board belongs to the team, not management, making it a tool for coordination rather than surveillance.↵:::↵:::anote{title="🚦 Work-in-Progress Limits"}↵Maximum items per stage↵Prevents overload↵Forces completion before starting new work↵Improves flow↵WIP limits are Kanban's secret weapon against the multitasking trap.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: By capping how many items can be in progress simultaneously, WIP limits force teams to finish work before starting new work.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: This constraint feels uncomfortable at first—developers hate being blocked—but it exposes systemic problems that multitasking masks.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: When you can't start new work because you've hit your WIP limit, you're forced to help finish existing work or fix the bottleneck causing the backup.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: This collaboration improves flow and reduces cycle time far more than everyone working on separate tasks ever could.↵:::↵:::anote{title="🌊 Flow Management"}↵No fixed iterations↵Work pulled when capacity available↵Continuous delivery↵Optimize cycle time↵Flow management prioritizes throughput over batching.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Without sprint boundaries, work flows continuously from backlog to done, getting deployed as soon as it's ready.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: This pull-based system means work starts when the team has capacity, not when a sprint begins.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Teams measure cycle time—how long from start to finish—and optimize for speed.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: This approach aligns perfectly with continuous deployment, where the goal is getting value to users as quickly as possible.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Flow management also handles variable work sizes naturally—small fixes don't wait for sprint planning, and large features don't artificially squeeze into sprint boundaries.↵:::↵:::anote{title="📈 Continuous Improvement"}↵Measure and optimize flow↵Identify bottlenecks↵Experiment with process changes↵Evolve based on data↵Continuous improvement in Kanban is data-driven rather than ceremony-driven.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Teams measure cycle time, throughput, and flow efficiency, using metrics to identify where the process breaks down.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: When data shows testing is a bottleneck, the team experiments with solutions—adding testers, automating tests, or shifting testing left.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: These experiments are small and reversible, making improvement low-risk.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Unlike retrospectives that happen every two weeks, Kanban improvement is ongoing—when you spot a problem, you fix it immediately.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: This evolutionary approach means the process constantly adapts to changing conditions without waiting for scheduled improvement sessions.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: The frameworks embody different philosophies:↵:::tip{title="Core Philosophy"}↵**Scrum: Predictability Through Rhythm**↵Regular cadence creates stability↵Commitment drives completion↵Ceremonies ensure coordination↵Velocity enables planning↵Best for: Predictable delivery schedules↵**Kanban: Efficiency Through Flow**↵Continuous flow maximizes throughput↵WIP limits prevent waste↵Metrics drive optimization↵Flexibility enables responsiveness↵Best for: Unpredictable work arrival↵Neither philosophy is inherently better.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: They optimize for different outcomes.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Scrum optimizes for predictability and team coordination.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Kanban optimizes for flow and responsiveness.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Scrum excels in specific contexts.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Understanding these contexts helps you decide if Scrum fits your situation.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Teams building products benefit from Scrum's structure:↵:::success{title="Scrum Strengths for Product Teams"}↵**Clear Planning Cycles**↵Sprint planning aligns team on goals↵Product owner prioritizes features↵Team estimates and commits↵Stakeholders know what to expect↵**Regular Delivery Rhythm**↵Demo working software every sprint↵Gather feedback consistently↵Iterate based on learning↵Build trust with stakeholders↵**Team Coordination**↵Daily standups synchronize work↵Sprint reviews align with stakeholders↵Retrospectives improve process↵Shared commitment builds cohesion↵A product team building a SaaS platform fits Scrum naturally.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Features can be planned in sprints.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Stakeholders attend sprint reviews.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: The team iterates based on feedback.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: The rhythm creates predictability that helps everyone plan.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Scrum assumes stable teams:↵:::anote{title="👥 Team Stability Requirements"}↵**Why Stability Matters**↵Velocity depends on consistent team↵Ceremonies assume same participants↵Team dynamics develop over time↵Estimation accuracy improves with stability↵**What Happens Without Stability**↵Velocity becomes meaningless↵Ceremonies feel wasteful↵Team doesn't gel↵Scrum overhead without benefits↵If your team composition changes frequently—contractors rotating in and out, team members shared across projects—Scrum's overhead may not pay off.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: The framework assumes the team stays together long enough to develop rhythm and improve.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Organizations needing predictable delivery schedules benefit from Scrum:↵:::tip{title="📅 Predictability Benefits"}↵**Stakeholder Management**↵Sprint reviews provide regular updates↵Velocity enables forecasting↵Roadmaps based on sprint capacity↵Reduces "when will it be done" questions↵**Dependency Coordination**↵Other teams plan around sprint boundaries↵Integration points at sprint ends↵Synchronized releases↵Reduces coordination overhead↵If marketing needs to plan campaigns, sales needs to commit to customers, or other teams depend on your deliverables, Scrum's predictability helps.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: The sprint boundary provides a coordination point.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Kanban excels in different contexts.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Recognizing these helps you identify when Kanban fits better than Scrum.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Teams handling support tickets or maintenance benefit from Kanban's flexibility:↵:::success{title="Kanban Strengths for Support Teams"}↵**Unpredictable Work Arrival**↵Tickets arrive continuously↵Priorities change based on severity↵No artificial sprint boundaries↵Respond immediately to urgent issues↵**Variable Work Size**↵Some tickets take minutes↵Others take days↵No need to estimate everything↵Focus on completing work, not planning↵**Continuous Delivery**↵Fix deployed as soon as ready↵No waiting for sprint end↵Faster resolution for customers↵Reduced work-in-progress↵A support team can't plan two weeks of work in advance.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Urgent issues arrive unpredictably.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Kanban's pull system handles this naturally.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Work gets done when capacity is available, without artificial sprint boundaries.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Teams deploying multiple times daily benefit from Kanban:↵:::anote{title="Continuous Deployment Fit"}↵**No Sprint Boundaries**↵Deploy whenever feature is ready↵No waiting for sprint end↵Faster time to market↵Reduced batch size↵**Flow Optimization**↵Measure cycle time↵Identify bottlenecks↵Optimize deployment pipeline↵Continuous improvement↵**Feature Flags**↵Deploy incomplete features↵Enable when ready↵Decouple deployment from release↵Kanban's flexibility enables this↵If you're deploying to production multiple times per day, sprint boundaries feel artificial.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Why wait for sprint end to release a completed feature?

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Kanban's continuous flow aligns better with continuous deployment.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: When priorities change frequently, Kanban's flexibility helps:↵:::tip{title="🔀 Handling Priority Changes"}↵**No Sprint Commitment**↵Reprioritize anytime↵Pull highest priority work next↵No "wait until next sprint"↵Respond to market changes quickly↵**Reduced Planning Overhead**↵No sprint planning ceremony↵Just-in-time prioritization↵Less time in meetings↵More time delivering value↵If your product manager changes priorities daily based on customer feedback or market conditions, Scrum's sprint commitment becomes a constraint.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Kanban lets you pivot immediately without breaking commitments.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Many teams combine Scrum and Kanban elements, creating Scrumban:

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Scrumban takes the best of both frameworks:↵:::anote{title="🔀 Scrumban Elements"}↵**From Scrum**↵Sprint planning for coordination↵Daily standups for synchronization↵Retrospectives for improvement↵Optional sprint reviews↵**From Kanban**↵Kanban board for visualization↵WIP limits to prevent overload↵Continuous delivery within sprint↵Flow metrics for optimization↵**The Combination**↵Plan work in sprints↵Manage flow with Kanban↵Deploy continuously↵Review and improve regularly↵Scrumban provides structure without rigidity.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: You get Scrum's coordination benefits and Kanban's flow optimization.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Scrumban works well in specific situations:↵:::success{title="Scrumban Sweet Spots"}↵**Transitioning from Scrum**↵Team comfortable with Scrum↵Want more flexibility↵Keep ceremonies, add flow management↵Gradual evolution↵**Mixed Work Types**↵Planned feature development↵Unplanned support work↵Sprints for features↵Kanban for support↵**Mature Teams**↵Understand both frameworks↵Can handle complexity↵Want optimization↵Don't need strict structure↵A team building features while handling production support might use Scrumban.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Sprint planning for features, Kanban board for all work, WIP limits to prevent overload, continuous deployment when ready.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Combining frameworks can create problems:↵:::error{title="Scrumban Pitfalls"}↵**Complexity Overload**↵Too many rules from both frameworks↵Team confused about process↵Overhead without benefits↵Simpler approach would work better↵**Cherry-Picking Without Understanding**↵Taking ceremonies without principles↵Cargo cult Scrumban↵Missing the point of both frameworks↵Creating bureaucracy↵**Avoiding Commitment**↵Using Kanban flexibility to avoid planning↵No sprint goals or focus↵Losing Scrum's benefits↵Not gaining Kanban's either↵Don't combine frameworks just because you can.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Understand why you're taking elements from each.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: If you can't articulate the benefit, you're probably adding complexity without value.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Teams make predictable mistakes with both Scrum and Kanban:

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Scrum's structure can be misused:↵:::error{title="Scrum Anti-Patterns"}↵**Sprint as Mini-Waterfall**↵Design sprint, then coding sprint, then testing sprint↵No working software until multiple sprints↵Missing iterative development point↵Waterfall with shorter phases↵**Velocity as Performance Metric**↵Management tracks velocity↵Teams inflate estimates↵Gaming the system↵Velocity becomes meaningless↵**Rigid Sprint Commitment**↵Can't change anything mid-sprint↵Even when priorities shift dramatically↵Process over outcomes↵Losing agility↵**Ceremony Theater**↵Going through motions without purpose↵Standups as status reports↵Retrospectives without action↵Meetings for meetings' sake↵These mistakes turn Scrum into bureaucracy.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: The framework becomes the goal instead of a tool for delivering value.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Kanban's flexibility can be misused:↵:::error{title="Kanban Anti-Patterns"}↵**No WIP Limits**↵Board shows all work↵But no limits on work-in-progress↵Team overloaded↵Missing Kanban's core benefit↵**Lack of Prioritization**↵Everything on the board↵No clear priorities↵Team picks randomly↵Flexibility becomes chaos↵**No Flow Metrics**↵Using Kanban board↵But not measuring cycle time↵Can't identify bottlenecks↵Missing improvement opportunities↵**Avoiding Planning**↵"We're Kanban, we don't plan"↵No strategic direction↵Reactive instead of proactive↵Flexibility as excuse for lack of vision↵These mistakes turn Kanban into chaos.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: The flexibility becomes an excuse for lack of discipline.↵:::

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: How do you decide between Scrum and Kanban?

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Ask these questions:

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Use this framework to guide your choice:↵:::tip{title="Decision Questions"}↵**Choose Scrum If:**↵Team is new to Agile (structure helps)↵Stakeholders need predictability↵Team composition is stable↵Work can be planned in iterations↵Product development focus↵Need coordination with other teams↵**Choose Kanban If:**↵Work arrives unpredictably↵Priorities change frequently↵Team does support/maintenance↵Continuous deployment environment↵Team experienced with Agile↵Want to optimize flow↵**Choose Scrumban If:**↵Mixed work types (planned + unplanned)↵Want structure with flexibility↵Team comfortable with both frameworks↵Transitioning from Scrum to more flow↵Need coordination but also responsiveness↵No framework is perfect for every situation.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: A support team handling customer issues used Kanban effectively:↵:::anote{title="🎫 Customer Support Team"}↵**Context**↵4 engineers handling production issues↵Tickets arrive unpredictably↵Severity ranges from minor to critical↵Need fast response times↵**Kanban Implementation**↵Board: Backlog → In Progress → Review → Done↵WIP limit: 2 items per person↵Priority: Severity-based↵Deploy fixes immediately when ready↵Weekly retrospectives↵**Why It Worked**↵Unpredictable work arrival↵Variable work size↵No artificial sprint boundaries↵Fast response to urgent issues↵Continuous improvement through metrics↵The team responded quickly to issues.

sentences.text: A platform team supporting product teams used Scrumban:↵:::anote{title="🛠️ Platform Team"}↵**Context**↵5 engineers building internal tools↵Planned feature development↵Unplanned support requests↵Need both predictability and responsiveness↵**Scrumban Implementation**↵2-week sprints for planning↵Kanban board for all work↵WIP limits: 3 items in progress↵Deploy continuously↵Sprint reviews and retrospectives↵**Why It Worked**↵Sprint planning for feature coordination↵Kanban flexibility for support requests↵WIP limits prevented overload↵Continuous deployment for fast delivery↵Best of both frameworks↵The team planned features in sprints but handled support requests immediately.

sentences.text: Scrum and Kanban aren't competing frameworks—they're tools for different contexts.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Scrum provides structure through time-boxed iterations, defined roles, and regular ceremonies.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: This structure helps teams new to Agile, teams needing predictability, and teams building products with stable composition.↵Kanban provides flexibility through continuous flow, WIP limits, and visual management.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: This flexibility helps teams handling unpredictable work, teams deploying continuously, and teams needing to respond quickly to changing priorities.↵Neither framework is universally superior.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Scrum excels when you need predictability and coordination.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Scrumban combines elements when you need both.↵Common mistakes with Scrum include treating sprints as mini-waterfalls, using velocity as a performance metric, and performing ceremonies without purpose.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Common mistakes with Kanban include skipping WIP limits, avoiding prioritization, and using flexibility as an excuse for lack of planning.↵The decision between frameworks depends on your context.

sourceRef.title: Kanban vs Scrum: Choosing the Right Agile Framework

sentences.text: Ask whether your work is predictable or unpredictable, whether your team is stable or changing, whether you need coordination or responsiveness.
